captions.text: Imagine a three hundred rupee refund.
Simple, right?
Now the same success notification arrives three times.
A naive backend records nine hundred rupees.
Not three payouts. Just one very wrong number.
And that’s before notifications start going missing or contradicting each other.
That’s why I built HISAAB.
It’s a Python backend using FastAPI.
Applications register refunds and send notifications through an authenticated API.
HISAAB handles duplicates, stores evidence using SQLite transactions and returns a refund status.
The dashboard?
That’s just a demo.
Watch this.
First notification: both processors show three hundred rupees.
Second: the naive processor says six hundred.
Third: nine hundred.
HISAAB? Still three hundred.
Three deliveries. One event. One correctly recorded refund.
What if a notification never arrives?
HISAAB keeps the outcome unknown until a simulated provider lookup supplies evidence.
And when success and failure disagree, it doesn’t guess.
It keeps both claims under review.
I also built a Hyperswitch webhook adapter.
This signed sample goes through the actual HTTP endpoint.
Duplicates leave the total unchanged, and invalid signatures get rejected.
It’s a local test, not a live provider delivery.
Alan helped me build this in smaller checkpoints.
Here’s the integration API task, the duplicate-handling test and its Git commits.
Independent review caught a few gaps.
I brought these findings back to Alan and verified the fixes with regression tests.
HISAAB. Ek refund. Sau nakhre.
Every refund accounted for.

scenes.title: Test · Count the same success event once
scenes.label: GENUINE TEST SOURCE Â· NOT AN EXECUTION
scenes.text:
def test_repeated_success_notifications_confirm_one_amount(client):
    ws = workspace(client)["workspace_id"]
    client.post(
        "/v1/workspaces/%s/refunds" % ws,
        json={"refund_id": "R1", "amount_paise": 30_000},
        headers=auth(),
    )
    payload = {
        "event_id": "E8",
        "refund_id": "R1",
        "status": "succeeded",
        "amount_paise": 30_000,
    }

    first = client.post(
        "/v1/workspaces/%s/deliveries" % ws,
        json=dict(payload, attempt_id="a1"),
        headers=auth(),
    )
    second = client.post(
        "/v1/workspaces/%s/deliveries" % ws,
        json=dict(payload, attempt_id="a2"),
        headers=auth(),
    )

    assert first.json()["outcome"] == "accepted"
    assert second.json()["outcome"] == "duplicate_event"

    status = client.get("/v1/workspaces/%s" % ws, headers=auth()).json()
    assert status["totals"]["confirmed_paise"] == 30_000

scenes.text:
ac20202 — historical checkpoint

Expose the integration service over an authenticated API

Four routes under /v1 for a trusted backend: create a workspace, register a refund, submit a normalized delivery, and read protected status with evidence. The demo routes and pages are untouched.

Bodies are strict. Money must be a positive JSON integer, so strings, floats and booleans are rejected. Identifiers are bounded to 64 characters, refunds per workspace are bounded to 50, unknown fields are refused, and only pending, succeeded and failed are accepted as statuses. Delivery origin is fixed to webhook on the server so a caller cannot claim a lookup happened.

Full original body: video/historical-commit.txt
Historical checks are not today’s test count.
